props.title: Ancient Evil: Scream of the Mummy
props.initialSlug: College students awaken a vengeful mummy's curse

sections.content: Let's dive into one of the more obscure entries in the direct-to-video horror boom of the early 2000s. Ancient Evil: Scream of the Mummy represents the bottom-tier of mummy horror films, arriving well after Tale of the Mummy (1998) and before the big-budget The Mummy Returns (2001). This ultra-low-budget attempt fails to capture any of the atmospheric dread of classic mummy films like The Mummy (1932) with Boris Karloff or even the pulpy fun of the Brendan Fraser-led The Mummy (1999).

sections.content: The direct-to-video horror market of the late 1990s and early 2000s was flooded with micro-budget knockoffs trying to capitalize on theatrical releases. Films like Bram Stoker's Legend of the Mummy (1998) and Russell Mulcahy's Tale of the Mummy (1998) attempted to modernize the ancient Egyptian horror subgenre with varying degrees of success, though none achieved the mainstream appeal of Stephen Sommers' blockbuster approach. SUBHEAD: The Decline of Mummy Horror

The mummy subgenre has struggled to evolve beyond its classic roots, with even big-budget attempts like The Mummy (2017) starring Tom Cruise failing to resonate with audiences. The most successful modern takes tend to be those that embrace either pure horror like Under Wraps (1997) or pure adventure like The Scorpion King (2002), rather than trying to straddle both genres awkwardly like Ancient Evil: Scream of the Mummy attempts.
